name: Mauve Taupe
lede: Mauve Taupe is a dusty, muted rose-brown on the dark side of the [[mauve]] family, dated by Maerz and Paul to about 1925 and confirmed in 1955 by the ISCC-NBS system, which lists it a close 1.1 units from its own "dark reddish gray" block.

sections.title: A dark mauve, many aliases
sections.body: Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates Mauve Taupe to about 1925, plate 7 C 8 [1]. The ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 attach a long run of other trade names to the very same block, among them Ashes of Rose, Aztec Maroon, Cineraria and Claret Cup, each a separate marketer's name landing on the same perceptual point [1]. The books held in color-kb do not mention "Mauve Taupe" itself [4]. Its nearest distinct neighbor by our graph is [[rose-dust]], 3.3 units off and described as "more vivid" [3]. Despite the modifier *taupe*, which usually names a flatter grey-brown, this color keeps real purple in it: hue angle 1.2 degrees, chroma 22.5, than to any grey [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Mauve Taupe in 30 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.1 percent, as photographed, mostly in works from the 1900s onward [2]. On the canvases where it does appear, it shares space with plain [[mauve]] far more than chance alone would predict, a lift of over 150 times the base rate, which argues the two were often used as a pair [3]. Counts are computed matches on varnished, photographed canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
